author: Mark Atwood
text: FRAMING CORRECTION 2026-05-12 (Mark, interactive after framing recalibration). The 2026-05-12 18:12 WONTFIX rationale carried wrong-frame supporting arguments that need to be surfaced for potential re-examination of the decision itself. WRONG-FRAME ELEMENTS in the closure: (2) 'Smallest dependency surface wins for a reference, not authoritative crate' -- this is YAGNI dressed as principle. Smallest-surface is a post-launch optimization, not a prelaunch architectural criterion. (1) 'PKIX-apmt's wire-format decision deferred 7 days' is now stale (apmt un-deferred under correct framing). SUBSTANTIVE QUESTION NOT ENGAGED in the original session: what does pkix-lint-cabf look like when complete? Two architectural candidates: (A) Comprehensive CA/B Forum BR coverage that matches or approaches zlint's scope (~700 lints across TLS BR / S/MIME BR / Code Signing BR). Hand-authoring this is intractable in practice; comprehensive coverage requires mirroring zlint's living catalog. (B) Small curated reference set of marquee BR violations (~10-30 lints). Hand-authoring works here; mirroring is overkill. The choice between A and B is the actual architectural decision, and it wasn't asked. Mark picked 'abandon zlint mirroring' which implicitly chose B. Under the correct framing he might still choose B (small reference set is a legitimate design for a 'reference, not authoritative' crate). But the question deserves to be asked explicitly. STANDS (substantive in the closure): (3) zlint+pkilint as differential oracles (PKIX-hbzo.1) are independently valuable -- arguably more valuable if pkix-lint-cabf is hand-authored, since divergence reveals interpretation bugs the shared-upstream model would hide. Trade-offs paragraph (ongoing authorial burden, loses tracking-upstream benefit) is substantive. Decision pending Mark's response to the surfaced question.
